title: When to extract a custom Hook

slides.say: You do not need a custom Hook for every bit of duplicate code. Wrapping one use state call is probably unnecessary.

slides.text: Writing an Effect? Consider wrapping it in a custom Hook.
slides.say: But whenever you write an Effect, consider wrapping it in a custom Hook. It communicates intent and data flow clearly.
Here two fetching Effects become use data. You feed a URL in, and get data out. With time, most Effects end up in custom Hooks.
Keep Hooks focused on concrete use cases, like use data or use chat room. Avoid lifecycle wrappers like use mount or use effect once.
